as_told.title: Solon's Atlantis account and Meltwater Pulse 1B

plain: This story is about Atlantis, the lost island civilisation described by the ancient Greek philosopher Plato in two of his dialogues, the Timaeus and the Critias. A researcher of ancient catastrophes named Randall Carlson points out that Plato dates Atlantis to 9,000 years before the Athenian lawmaker Solon travelled to Egypt, which Carlson puts at 600 BC, so about 9600 BC. In the story's framing, that date lines up with the end of the Younger Dryas, a sudden cold spell near the close of the last ice age, and with Meltwater Pulse 1B, a fast rise in sea level as ice melted. A podcast host named Jesse Michels also tells it, crediting a writer named Graham Hancock and saying the account was told in 600 BC and is recorded in the Timaeus and Critias, with the Egyptian city of Sais as the place. People tell it because, if true, Plato's tale would preserve a real memory of a civilisation lost to a global disaster.
